record.original_question:
Does the Lorentz space L_{p,q} have a greedy basis when p 
eq q?

evidence.quote: Problem 14.4. Does the Lorentz space Lp,q have a greedy basis if p 6= q?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a non-atomic $\sigma$-finite measure space (for instance $[0,1]$ or $[0,\infty)$ with Lebesgue measure). For a measurable function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{C}$, let $f^{*}:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ denote its non-increasing rearrangement, defined by $f^{*}(t)=\inf\{s\ge 0:\mu(\{|f|>s\})\le t\}$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $1\le q<\infty$, the Lorentz space $L_{p,q}(\Omega)$ consists of all measurable $f$ such that
$$\|f\|_{p,q}:=\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl(t^{1/p}f^{*}(t)\bigr)^{q}\,\frac{dt}{t}\right)^{1/q}<\infty,$$
with the obvious modification $\|f\|_{p,\infty}=\sup_{t>0}t^{1/p}f^{*}(t)$ when $q=\infty$.

A Schauder basis $(e_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of a Banach space $X$ is called \emph{greedy} if there exists a constant $C\ge 1$ such that for every $x\in X$ and every $m\in\mathbb{N}$,
$$\|x-G_m(x)\|\le C\,\inf\Bigl\{\bigl\|x-\sum_{n\in A}a_n e_n\bigr\|:|A|=m,\ a_n\in\mathbb{C}\Bigr\},$$
where $G_m(x)$ is any $m$-term greedy approximation obtained by keeping $m$ of the largest (in modulus) coefficients in the expansion $x=\sum_n e_n^{*}(x)e_n$. Equivalently (Konyagin–Temlyakov), a basis is greedy if and only if it is unconditional and democratic.

\textbf{Problem.} Suppose $1<p<\infty$, $1\le q\le\infty$, and $p\neq q$. Does the Lorentz space $L_{p,q}(\Omega)$ admit a greedy basis?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches in the recent literature on greedy and almost greedy bases (including 2022–2025 work on Lorentz spaces and embeddings induced by almost greedy bases, and the 2024 survey "Twenty-five years of greedy bases") do not report a construction of a greedy basis for $L_{p,q}$ with $p\ne q$, nor a proof that none exists. Related results concern almost greedy bases in mixed-norm and Besov-type spaces and Lorentz sequence spaces, but the question for the function-space $L_{p,q}$ appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Twenty-five years of greedy bases
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of greedy basis theory mentioning existence/nonexistence of greedy bases in various classical function spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey does not list a resolution of the existence of a greedy basis in $L_{p,q}$ for $p\ne q$.

status_evidence.title: Lorentz spaces and embeddings induced by almost greedy bases in superreflexive Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies embeddings between Banach spaces and Lorentz sequence spaces using almost greedy bases.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on almost greedy bases and Lorentz sequence spaces rather than constructing greedy bases in $L_{p,q}$.

status_evidence.title: Approximation spaces, greedy classes and Lorentz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: 2024–2025 paper on approximation spaces and Lorentz spaces in the context of greedy approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research; no claim of constructing a greedy basis in $L_{p,q}$ with $p\ne q$.
